title: Can published acoustic distance predict zebra-finch probe choices?

source_paper.title: Bird song comparison using deep learning trained from avian perceptual judgments

model: Single-predictor logistic regression; response is bird choosing right rather than left; predictor is Luscinia distance(left, probe) minus distance(right, probe).
scope: Probe trials from documented CSV; repeated trials grouped by bird. This is an explanatory baseline, not a reproduction of the paper deep-learning model.
limitations: Split is by bird, but stimuli may overlap between train/test birds.
Repeated choices for the same stimulus are not independent; bootstrap resamples held-out birds.
Luscinia distance is one published acoustic metric, not a direct measure of neural representation or communication meaning.
Missing distance pairs are dropped; coverage and excluded counts are reported.
Behavioral choice is used; no brain recordings are modeled.
The model is a transparent statistical baseline and does not claim to outperform the paper.
